newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Zhejiang Power plans to issue A, B shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Zhejiang Power plans to issue A, B shares.

text.p: Zhejiang Southeast Electric Power Co Ltd has applied to the China Securities Regulatory Commission to issue 150 million A shares next year and list them on the Shanghai bourse, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

The company, based in Hangzhou, capital of the southeast province of Zhejiang, has also applied to the Securities Commission of the State Council to issue 400 million B shares and list the stock in Shanghai, the spokesman told the China Securities Bulletin, a Hong Kong-based newsletter.
He said the firm expected to launch the A share issue before issuing the B shares.
Zhejiang Provincial Securities Co Ltd will be the lead underwriter for the offers, with BZW Securities International the coordinator for the B share issue, he said.

Southeast plans to use proceeds from the offers to finance continuing construction of the 3.9 billion yuan Zhejiang Taizhou Power Plant, with two 330,000-kw generators, and to buy several other Zhejiang-based power plants, the official said.
One generator at the Taizhou Plant has just become operational and the other will begin operations by the end of 1997.
Zhejiang Southeast has seven generators, including six each with a capacity of 125,000 kw. It mainly supplies electricity within Zhejiang province, the official said.
Zhejiang Southeast forecast unaudited per-share net of 0.40 yuan for 1996 based on current total share capital of 850 million shares which are owned by state companies.
The forecast roughly equals levels in the past two years, the official said without giving precise figures.
He said Southeast expected to produce 4.5 billion kw-hours of electricity this year and six billion in 1997.
